svg.aria-label: Boiler and double-acting steam engine (schematic). 1 Safety devices a boiler must have: safety valve (opens automatically and vents steam when the pressure passes the set value; check it regularly and never block it or weigh it down), pressure gauge (shows the pressure at all times; it usually reads gauge pressure, and absolute pressure equals gauge pressure plus about 0.1 MPa), water gauge (shows the water level at all times), water feed (can top up water while running). 2 Main parts of a steam engine: the boiler makes steam; in the cylinder, steam drives the piston back and forth; the steam valve (slide valve) sends steam to each side of the piston in turn; the crank and connecting rod turn back-and-forth motion into rotation; the flywheel smooths the rotation; the governor (centrifugal flyballs) automatically closes down the steam inlet when running too fast; the condenser (optional) turns exhaust steam back into water, lowering back pressure, raising efficiency and recovering water. 3 Double-acting: with the slide valve to the right, steam enters the left side and pushes the piston right while the right side exhausts; with the slide valve to the left, steam enters the right side and pushes the piston left while the left side exhausts: 2 power strokes per turn. 4 Why boilers explode: a boiler stores a large amount of high-pressure water above 100°C; if it bursts, the pressure drops at once and the hot water instantly boils into steam; 1 kg of water turned into steam at 100°C and 1 atm expands about 1700 times; never block or weigh down the safety valve; low water is the most dangerous: the metal above the firebox runs dry, overheats and weakens, and suddenly adding cold water can cause an immediate explosion; if the water is very low, put the fire out first and let the boiler cool slowly, do not add water at once; without professional design and testing, use only atmospheric or very-low-pressure equipment
svg.title: Boiler and steam engine

g.text: The boiler makes steam → the slide valve sends it to each side of the piston in turn
→ the crank and connecting rod turn back-and-forth motion into rotation
① Boiler: the safety devices it must have
Water too low → the metal above the firebox runs dry and overheats (see ④)
opens by itself and vents steam when
the pressure passes the set value;
check it regularly; never block it
✓ Water gauge: shows the water level
✓ Water feed: can top up while running
② Double-acting steam engine: main parts (section, piston moving right)
Cylinder and piston → steam drives the piston back and forth
Steam valve (slide valve) → sends steam to each side of the piston in turn
Crank and connecting rod → turn back-and-forth motion into rotation
Governor → closes down the steam inlet when running too fast (centrifugal flyballs)
Condenser (optional) → turns exhaust steam back into water: lowers back pressure,
raises efficiency and recovers the water
③ Double-acting: steam pushes each side in turn (2 power strokes per turn)
• A boiler stores a large amount of high-pressure water above 100°C: if it bursts,
the pressure drops at once and the hot water instantly boils into steam
(1 kg of water turned into steam at 100°C and 1 atm expands about 1700 times)
→ the bigger the boiler and the higher the pressure, the more violent the blast
• Never block or weigh down the safety valve; check it regularly
• Low water is the most dangerous: the metal above the firebox runs dry, overheats
and weakens; suddenly adding cold water now can cause an immediate explosion
→ If the water is very low, put the fire out first and let the boiler cool slowly;
do not add water at once
• Without professional design and testing, use only atmospheric or very-low-pressure equipment
